howToTell: The Waco F-series is smaller and slimmer, with a wide front cockpit seating two and a smoother fuselage; the Stearman has narrow tandem cockpits and a bulkier airframe.
The Travel Air has big overhanging 'elephant-ear' balanced ailerons and an earlier, boxier 1920s look; the Stearman has plain ailerons.

The Waco 10 is a 1920s barnstormer with a wide passenger cockpit under the upper wing ahead of the pilot, often with an OX-5 nose radiator; the Stearman has two narrow tandem cockpits and a bare radial.
The Taperwing's wings visibly taper toward the tips; the Stearman's wings are straight with constant chord.
The Meyers OTW is a much smaller, lighter biplane with a small radial; the Stearman is a large, heavy biplane with a big radial.
The Great Lakes is a small biplane with a cowled flat-four engine and a swept-back upper wing; the Stearman has a large bare radial.
The Fleet is a much smaller, lighter biplane with a small Kinner radial; the Stearman is large and heavy with a big radial.
The Fairchild KR is a small, light 1920s biplane with a small radial; the Stearman is much larger and heavier with a big radial.
The Yak-50 is a single-seater with a tailwheel and retractable main gear; the Yak-52 has two seats in tandem and a retractable tricycle undercarriage.
The Yak-55 is a single-seat mid-wing aerobatic monoplane with fixed gear and a tailwheel; the Yak-52 has two seats and retractable tricycle gear.
The CAP 10 is a low-wing taildragger with two seats side by side under a bubble canopy and a ventral fin; the Citabria is a high-wing tandem-seat aircraft.
The CAP 10 is a taildragger with a ventral fin under the tail and a bubble canopy; the DA20 has a nosewheel and a wider, flatter canopy.
The Monocoupe has a small radial engine and a distinctive reverse-curve rear fuselage; the Luscombe is all-metal with a flat-four engine and a smoother fuselage line.
